newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo-Mitsubishi U.S. unit incurs derivatives loss.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo-Mitsubishi U.S. unit incurs derivatives loss.

text.p: Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd said in a statement that its U.S. unit had posted an appraisal loss of around $50 million from taking positions in such instruments as U.S. interest rate swaps.
Tokyo-Mitsubishi Derivative Products (USA), after having closed those positions, posted an after-tax loss of $83 million at its book closing in December, 1996, the statement said.
The bank said its U.S. unit has already informed U.S. and Japanese authorities of the losses.

After conducting a thorough internal investigation, the bank confirmed that its U.S. unit had not broken any laws, regulations or internal rules, and thus regulators were not involved, the statement said.
The losses surfaced after a review of the unit's portfolio appraisal model, which had overestimated the market value of the position, it said.

In the Japanese Government Bond (JGB) market, bonds were bought to the day's highs in mid-afternoon on a rumour that the Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi had suffered a significant loss through derivatives trading, traders said.
The rumour helped drag down the bank's shares to as low as 1,970 yen in the Thursday afternoon session.
BOT-Mitsubishi's shares ended down 40 yen at 2,050 yen.
Commenting on the loss, Walter Altherr, senior financial analyst at Jardine Fleming Securities, said; "It's not an enormous amount of money."
"It may be big for the U.S. unit, but I don't think it's big for the group."
He said that it would not cause "the slightest" problem for the bank's financial health.
